newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Treasurer says cuts size of pension bond sale.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Treasurer says cuts size of pension bond sale.

text.p: New Jersey Treasurer Brian Clymer said Monday the state has reduced the size of its proposed taxable pension obligation bond deal to $2.9 billion from $3.4 billion.

Clymer, speaking at a press conference outlining the proposed sale, said the state was able to reduce the size of the bond deal by drawing more from the pension system's existing surplus. The state has proposed the bond sale to fully fund the state's $4.2 billion unfunded pension liability.
Clymer said he expects legislation required for the taxable bond deal to be introduced "as soon as possible."
For the plan to work, he said, the bonds must be sold before June 30, the end of the fiscal year.
Samuel Corliss, a managing at Merrill Lynch & Co, the senior manager for the bond offering, told reporters he expects the market to handle the deal well.

"Transactions of this size are really rather easily accommodated in this market," Corliss said, noting that $3.4 trillion of taxable debt has been sold over the last four years compared $800 billion of tax-exempt debt over the same period.
Corliss said no decision has been made about how much of New Jersey's sale would be sold overseas, but he said a domestic road show would require about three weeks.
The legislature, which has raised questions about whether such a large debt issuance would be prudent, must approve two bills for the deal to proceed.
In the first, the legislature must agree to allow $1.3 billion of the pension system's existing surplus to be counted towards lowering the undfunded liability.

In the second, it must approve the sale of the bonds themselves. The sale must take place before June 30 because the state is counting on the deal for about $647 million of budget savings in fiscal years 1997 and 1998.
